evidence.location: Complete analysis/TE-U2-three-workloads.md sections 6-8; complete workload_calculations.py; relevant frozen calculation-results.json ledgers and sensitivities; original token_economics_en.json and assigned requirements.
evidence.basis: I independently reconstructed the support, documents and agent cohorts from the stated finite paths, source rates and human/tool allowances using Decimal, without importing or running the author's script. All 65 numerical/ledger comparisons performed match the frozen results; these are arithmetic comparisons within three scenarios, not empirical tests of model quality. Support totals are 243.11/994 and 184.15/996; document-set bills are 3.000, 1.416, 0.732 and 1.668 after the specified edits; agent totals are 789.20/96 and 765.84/97. Initial, retry, fallback, unsuccessful human work, and accepted/unresolved denominators are consistently counted. Wage/quality/retry/review sensitivities and the Gemini 200K discontinuity also agree. One output-sensitivity label omits a necessary fixed-input assumption; the arithmetic itself is not wrong. Price checks used the original TE05 PDF page 1, including visual inspection of the stored page image: effective 2026-10-22, USD/MTok, Claude API Standard Global, Haiku <=100K and Sonnet/Opus all-context rows. TE-S03 original server Markdown confirms Gemini 2.5 Pro/Flash standard input, output, cached-read and storage rates; its December routing changes were not used. Current Claude primary cache documentation confirms request-start TTL renewal, incremental prefix accounting, minimum sizes, and model-specific read prices; the 60-minute cache correctly hits at minute 90 after use at 34. Current Claude thinking documentation confirms reasoning is billed within output. The historical GPT-4o-mini announcement confirms July 18, 2024 launch rates. TE11 and TE-S07 confirm successful Search/Fetch billing and nonbillable failure definitions; TE07 confirms separate OpenAI search-call and content-token meters. TE-S19 supports the separate Gemini explicit-storage treatment. TE23's September 23 outcome definitions, TE18 v2 abstract/results and METR's TE-S18 v1 design/results plus TE20 methodology update support the bounded productivity discussion. Performance, traffic, latency and labor numbers are explicitly scenarios rather than measured model outcomes. Source reading was confined to these consequential passages; unrelated training/hosting/value-capture sources attached to the assignment were not reassessed. This is evidence review of TE-U2 only, not whole-report acceptance.

findings.location: Section 8 output sensitivity table and paragraph beginning 'Output compression has value'; workload_calculations.py trajectory(... output_scale) and agent_output
findings.basis: R_TASK requires auditable sensitivity assumptions and context growth. The sensitivity multiplies generated output while keeping every input context and cached-prefix count fixed; the prose says quality is held fixed but does not identify the fixed-input billing counterfactual. At 4x output, the first baseline call has 4K input and 8K output, while the next remains 8K input. An append-only trajectory retaining that output would already require at least 12K input before new tool/user content. Thus 9.0383 per accepted task is correct for the code's direct output-charge perturbation, but is not the cost of that fully retained workflow. Either label the table explicitly as a partial output-bill sensitivity with input histories, cache ledgers and paths held fixed (and no claim to model the induced context growth), or propagate retained output through later input/cache/compaction costs under stated assumptions. A label clarification is sufficient for this local defect; no new model experiment is requested.
